data.title: fix(spike): add STAThread and SynchronizationContext to WebView2 flicker spike

epic.spec:
# fix(spike): Add STAThread and SynchronizationContext to WebView2 Flicker Spike

## Problem

The spike app at `spike/WebView2FlickerSpike/Program.cs` uses C# top-level statements, which cannot carry the `[STAThread]` attribute. The .NET runtime defaults to MTA (Multi-Threaded Apartment). When WebView2 or DComp COM objects are created, they require STA, causing:

```
System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException: 'Cannot change thread mode after it is set. (0x80010106 (RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE))'
```

Additionally, the spike's raw Win32 message loop (`GetMessage`/`DispatchMessage` in `MainWindow.cs`) does not install a `SynchronizationContext`, so `async` continuations from `FireAndForget` methods resume on MTA threadpool threads — a latent threading bug even after the STA fix.

## Scope

- Convert `Program.cs` from top-level statements to explicit `static void Main()` with `[STAThread]`
- Install a `SynchronizationContext` so async continuations marshal back to the STA/UI thread
- Handle `DisposeAsync` in the now-synchronous `Main`
- Spike-only change — no impact on library, test app, or CI

## Quick commands

```bash
# Build the spike
dotnet build spike/WebView2FlickerSpike/WebView2FlickerSpike.csproj

# Run the spike (Windows only — requires WebView2 Runtime)
dotnet run --project spike/WebView2FlickerSpike/WebView2FlickerSpike.csproj
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] Spike runs without `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE` COM exception
- [ ] `[STAThread]` attribute present on `Main()`
- [ ] Async continuations (from `FireAndForget`) execute on the STA/UI thread
- [ ] `DisposeAsync` cleanup still runs correctly
- [ ] No changes to files outside `spike/WebView2FlickerSpike/`

## Key context

- `async Task Main()` with `[STAThread]` does NOT work — continuations resume on MTA threadpool threads (dotnet/runtime#73099). Must use synchronous `void Main()`.
- `WindowsFormsSynchronizationContext` is the simplest proven approach for raw Win32 message loops. Alternatively, a custom `SynchronizationContext` posting via `PostMessage` works but is more code.
- `MainWindow.FireAndForget` dispatches async WebView2 init — these continuations are the secondary threading concern.
- DComp COM interfaces in `DCompInterop.cs` (all `[ComImport]` with `InterfaceIsIUnknown`) are STA-affine.

## References

- `spike/WebView2FlickerSpike/Program.cs` — top-level statements, no `[STAThread]`
- `spike/WebView2FlickerSpike/MainWindow.cs:60-259` — Win32 message loop, `FireAndForget`
- `spike/WebView2FlickerSpike/DCompInterop.cs` — DComp COM interface definitions
- `MonacoEditorTestApp/Platforms/Desktop/Program.cs` — reference for correct `[STAThread]` usage
- dotnet/runtime#73099 — async Main + STAThread incompatibility

data.title: Convert spike Program.cs to STAThread Main with SynchronizationContext

tasks.spec:
# fn-16-fixspike-add-stathread-and.1 Convert spike Program.cs to STAThread Main with SynchronizationContext

## Description
Convert the spike's `Program.cs` from top-level statements to an explicit `[STAThread] static void Main()` and install a `SynchronizationContext` on the UI thread so async continuations from `FireAndForget` marshal back to STA.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `spike/WebView2FlickerSpike/Program.cs`, `spike/WebView2FlickerSpike/MainWindow.cs`

## Approach

- Follow the pattern at `MonacoEditorTestApp/Platforms/Desktop/Program.cs` for `[STAThread]` declaration
- Replace top-level statements with `class Program { [STAThread] static void Main() { ... } }`
- Must use synchronous `void Main()` — `async Task Main()` defeats `[STAThread]` (dotnet/runtime#73099)
- Install `SynchronizationContext` before the message loop so `await` continuations post back to STA. Two options:
  - `WindowsFormsSynchronizationContext.SetSynchronizationContext()` (simplest, requires `System.Windows.Forms` reference)
  - Custom `SynchronizationContext` that posts via Win32 `PostMessage` to the HWND (no extra dependency)
- Convert `await window.DisposeAsync()` to synchronous disposal (implementations in `MainWindow` are effectively sync)

## Key context

- `MainWindow.FireAndForget` in `MainWindow.cs` dispatches async WebView2 init — these continuations are the secondary threading concern after the STA fix
- The spike's Win32 message loop is a raw `GetMessage`/`DispatchMessage` loop — no WinForms `Application.Run` — so no built-in `SynchronizationContext` is installed
- DComp COM interfaces (`DCompInterop.cs`) are all STA-affine via `[ComImport]`
## Acceptance
- [ ] `Program.cs` has explicit `[STAThread] static void Main()` (no top-level statements)
- [ ] Spike runs without `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE` COM exception
- [ ] `SynchronizationContext.Current` is non-null on the UI thread before WebView2 init
- [ ] Async continuations from `FireAndForget` execute on the STA thread (verify via `Thread.CurrentThread.GetApartmentState() == ApartmentState.STA`)
- [ ] Window cleanup/disposal still executes correctly on exit
- [ ] No changes outside `spike/WebView2FlickerSpike/`
